_description: CropCare AI — Fertilizer Rules Knowledge Base. Disease-specific nutrient adjustments and dosage guidance based on agricultural extension recommendations.

Urea.general_dosage: 50–100 kg/acre depending on crop and soil test
Urea.application: Split application: 50% basal + 25% at 30 DAS + 25% at 60 DAS
safety_notes: Do not apply to waterlogged soil
Apply early morning or late evening to reduce volatilisation losses

DAP.application: Apply as basal dose mixed with soil at planting
safety_notes: Do not apply to alkaline soils (pH > 7.5) without amendment
Keep away from seed to avoid ammonia toxicity

MOP.general_dosage: 30–60 kg/acre depending on soil potassium status
MOP.application: Basal application mixed with soil; some split at flowering
safety_notes: Avoid in chloride-sensitive crops (e.g., tobacco, grapes)
Do not overapply — can cause salt injury
Avoid mixing with urea — chemical reaction reduces efficacy
Use soil test results to determine need
Do not apply with micronutrient mixes without compatibility check

NPK 20-20-20.general_dosage: 3–5 g/L for foliar spray; 2–4 kg/acre for fertigation
NPK 20-20-20.application: Foliar spray or drip fertigation during active growth
safety_notes: Spray in early morning or evening to avoid leaf burn
Do not mix with pesticides without compatibility check

Ammonium Sulphate.application: Basal or top-dressing; preferred for sulphur-deficient soils
safety_notes: Acidifies soil with repeated use — monitor soil pH
Keep away from direct seed contact

Apple.notes: Mature apple trees need higher K for fruit quality. Apply N in early spring and post-harvest. Avoid late-season N that delays dormancy.

Corn.notes: Corn is a heavy nitrogen feeder. Split N application: 1/3 basal + 1/3 at knee-high + 1/3 at tasseling. Zinc deficiency common in calcareous soils.

Potato.notes: Potato requires high K for tuber bulking and quality. Excess N can delay maturity and reduce dry matter. Apply P as basal dose.

Tomato.notes: Tomato needs high K during fruiting for colour development and firmness. Calcium is important to prevent blossom end rot. Avoid excess N during fruiting.

disease_nutrient_adjustments._description: Adjustments to nutrient recommendations when a specific disease is detected. These modify the base recommendation.

blight_diseases.reason: Excess nitrogen promotes lush, succulent growth that is highly susceptible to blight pathogens. Potassium strengthens cell walls and enhances plant immunity.
blight_diseases.specific_advice: Reduce nitrogen application by 20–30% from recommended. Increase potassium (K₂O) by 15–25%. Apply potassium sulphate (SOP) instead of MOP for better disease resistance.

fungal_leaf_spots.reason: Potassium and calcium strengthen cell walls, making leaves more resistant to fungal penetration. Moderate nitrogen avoids excessive leaf growth that retains moisture.
fungal_leaf_spots.specific_advice: Maintain nitrogen at lower end of recommended range. Apply calcium nitrate or gypsum for calcium supplementation. Use potassium sulphate for K.

fruit_rots.reason: Calcium reduces fruit susceptibility to rotting. Potassium improves overall fruit quality and plant defence.
fruit_rots.specific_advice: Apply calcium chloride (0.5%) foliar spray 3–4 times during fruit development. Ensure adequate K through soil application of MOP or SOP.

viral_diseases.reason: Virus-infected plants have impaired nutrient uptake and translocation. Supplemental micronutrients (Zn, Fe, Mn) and potassium can help maintain plant vigour and partial productivity.
viral_diseases.specific_advice: Apply foliar micronutrient spray (ZnSO₄ 0.5% + FeSO₄ 0.5%) every 15 days. Maintain normal NPK schedule but consider 10–15% extra K to support plant immunity.

pest_damage.reason: Well-nourished plants recover faster from mite damage. Silicon strengthens leaf cuticle, making it harder for mites to feed.
pest_damage.specific_advice: Apply potassium silicate (0.3%) foliar spray to strengthen leaf surfaces. Maintain balanced NPK nutrition to support recovery.

bacterial_diseases.reason: Excess nitrogen creates tender tissue that bacteria easily colonise. Calcium strengthens cell walls and pectin structures.
bacterial_diseases.specific_advice: Reduce N by 15–20%. Apply calcium nitrate or gypsum at 200–300 kg/ha. Avoid ammonium-based fertilizers.

healthy.reason: Plant is healthy — continue with standard fertilisation recommendations based on crop stage and soil test results.
healthy.specific_advice: No disease-specific adjustments needed. Follow the crop-specific base recommendations.

recommendations: Split nitrogen applications more frequently (3–4 splits)
Apply higher organic matter (FYM at 10–15 t/ha)

Loamy.nutrient_retention: Medium-Good — balanced water and nutrient holding
recommendations: Maintain organic matter with crop residue incorporation
Rich in K and Ca; may need less potassium
Apply gypsum if sodic; manage drainage carefully
Often deficient in N, P, and micronutrients (Zn, B)
Apply lime if pH < 5.5 to improve nutrient availability
Use SSP or rock phosphate for phosphorus

Clayey.nutrient_retention: High — holds water and nutrients well
recommendations: Apply potassium as MOP or SOP based on crop

safety_disclaimer: ⚠️ DISCLAIMER: These recommendations are for educational reference only. Actual fertiliser application should be based on soil testing results and local agricultural advisory. Always consult your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), agricultural extension officer, or certified agronomist before applying any treatments. Dosages may vary by region, season, crop variety, and soil conditions.
